description: Implement the generic runtime services that let ANY fabric producer (a cuneiform export, or any A2A/MCP app emitting koine contracts) participate — so ecosystem connectivity lives in agora's koine implementation, not in each app. This is the agora half of the 'apps are thin producers, agora bridges the data planes' decision (koine:40). Each service consumes/produces a RATIFIED koine contract and is generic over the producer: KGP knowledge sync (ADR-0006), KFT training-data admission -> trainer/lugh (fine-tuning.md), KINP resolution + grounding-pack ingestion (identity.md, grounding-pack.md). G2/G4 (KCB discovery registry, KINP resolver, provider-router) already EXIST in agora — the work there is confirming/exposing the client-facing surfaces a producer needs, not rebuilding. Behavioral reference (NOT to copy): the Argos repo at tag `fabric-reference` (~/Development/argos: bridge/, kcb_manifest.py, kgp_claim.py, kinp_curie.py, core/provider_router.py). agora gates on `make check`.
warmup: ls clients resolver registry trainer schemas

userStories.title: KGP knowledge sync: accept producer claims, deliver to a KGP consumer
userStories.description: A generic service that accepts KGP knowledge claims (RDF/PROV/JSON-LD per koine ADR-0006, keyed on the shared relation registry) from any producer over MCP/A2A and syncs/delivers them to a KGP consumer (pinakes, or any KGP endpoint). It is agnostic to WHICH app produced the claims — it validates against the koine relation registry + KGP shape and forwards by reference. No app-specific canonical mapping lives here (that is the producer's thin adapter, cuneiform:126). Reference for the claim/graph shape: Argos bridge/canonical_export.py + grounding.py at tag fabric-reference; the contract is koine ADR-0006 + registry/relations.tsv.
acceptanceCriteria: A generic KGP-sync surface accepts claims conformant to koine ADR-0006 + the relation registry from an arbitrary producer and delivers them to a configured KGP consumer, validating relations against registry/relations.tsv and rejecting unknown relations.
It is producer-agnostic (a test drives it with a synthetic non-Argos producer payload) and carries no app-specific canonicalization; `make check` green.

userStories.title: KFT dataset bridge: by-reference training-exhaust admission -> trainer/lugh
userStories.description: Implement the KFT data-plane bridge (fine-tuning.md §4): accept a producer's training-exhaust as a BY-REFERENCE dataset (KGP/KMI refs + a dataset-jsonl-header, never inlined), apply the NORMATIVE egress/license/trust gate, and submit a KFT finetune job to the trainer (lugh, or agora's own trainer for the general envelope). Reuse trainer/ + schemas/. This is where the 'training exhaust' an app emits becomes an actual finetune job, gated. Reference: Argos bridge/dataset_export.py at tag fabric-reference; contract is koine fine-tuning.md + the dataset-jsonl-header/finetune-job schemas + the e2e-finetune scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: The bridge admits a by-reference KFT dataset (dataset-jsonl-header, KGP/KMI refs), enforces the egress/license/trust gate (§4) — refusing an over-envelope or unlicensed dataset with a graded reason — and submits a finetune job to the trainer; a lugh-envelope job routes to lugh, an over-envelope one is refused/routed per KFT.
No training data is inlined (by-reference only); driven end-to-end by a test mirroring koine's e2e-finetune scenario; `make check` green.

userStories.title: KINP resolution + grounding-pack ingestion (query-time merge view)
userStories.description: Expose generic KINP identity resolution (identity.md): resolve identifiers, compute the merged-entity VIEW at query time from `same_as` claims (§4 — merge is a query-time view, never stored), and ingest a grounding-pack (grounding-pack.md) of world-knowledge a producer references for grounding. Grounding a mention to a canonical entity is a source-local-id `same_as` (per koine:40's locked decision — NO `mentions` relation), resolved here. Reuse resolver/. Reference: Argos bridge/grounding.py + grounding_pack.py + kinp_curie.py at tag fabric-reference; contract is koine identity.md + grounding-pack.md + registry (same_as).
acceptanceCriteria: A resolver surface dereferences a KINP identifier and returns the merged-entity view computed at query time from same_as claims (nothing stored merged), and ingests a grounding-pack per grounding-pack.md; unknown/ambiguous below-threshold cases emit nothing and queue for review (identity.md §11).
Grounding uses same_as only (no mentions relation), producer-agnostic; `make check` green.

userStories.title: Confirm the KCB-manifest + provider-router client surfaces a producer needs (G2/G4)
userStories.description: G2 (KCB discovery registry, KINP resolver) and G4 (provider-router) already exist in agora — DO NOT rebuild them. Confirm and, where thin, expose the CLIENT-facing surfaces a fabric producer needs: (a) publish/register a producer's KCB capability manifest to the discovery registry and be discoverable + dial-able (ADR-0001: registry returns addresses, peers dial direct, no proxy); (b) route a producer's OpenAI-compatible calls through the provider-router via a documented base-url/client (the thin client side of Argos core/provider_router.py). Add small client helpers/docs in clients/ only if a producer cannot already do this against the existing runtime. Reference: Argos kcb_manifest.py + provider_router.py at tag fabric-reference; koine capability-bus.md.
acceptanceCriteria: A producer can register a KCB capability manifest with agora's existing registry and be discovered + directly dialed (no proxying), and can route provider calls through the router via a documented client/base-url — demonstrated by a test, reusing the EXISTING registry/resolver/router (no reimplementation).
Any gap is closed with a thin client helper/doc in clients/, not a new runtime; `make check` green.
